panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (A, B). A: Left ultrasound panel explicitly labeled as showing hepatomegaly, which is part of the hepatosplenomegaly confirmed on abdominal ultrasonography in the beta-thalassemia major case. Hepatomegaly is a classic complication of beta-thalassemia major driven by iron overload and extramedullary hematopoiesis, but is not included in the provided findings vocabulary so is listed in proposed findings. B: Right ultrasound panel corresponding to splenic imaging demonstrating splenomegaly, which is the splenic component of the reported hepatosplenomegaly in the beta-thalassemia major case. Splenomegaly is a classic, well-documented manifestation of the disease and matches the provided findings vocabulary term beta_thalassemia_major_massive_splenomegaly.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: Axial CT of the same patient shows the captioned posterior mediastinal mass attributable to beta-thalassemia-related extramedullary hematopoietic myelolipoma. B: Axial MRI shows the posterior mediastinal paraspinal mass described in the beta-thalassemia major case. C: Coronal MRI visualizes the paraspinal/posterior mediastinal lesion in the beta-thalassemia major patient. D: H&E specimen of the lesion shows mature adipocytes and hematopoietic elements, matching the posterior mediastinal myelolipoma in the beta-thalassemia major case.
